openItems.explanation: The Q2 report as filed left out the June 26 bonus run: $55,500.00 of wages for 6 people. Paid Leave premiums of $627.15 and WA Cares premiums of $321.90 on those wages were not reported or paid. A person files an amended Q2 report.

Omar Rasmussen (E-1032) gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval on July 22, 2026, and payroll stopped the deductions from the July 24 payday. The rules point two ways. The Paid Leave toolkit says to stop from the exemption's effective date, October 1, 2026 (the first day of the quarter after approval), or the date of notice, whichever is later; RCW 50B.04.055(9) says employers may not deduct premiums after being notified of an approved exemption. The draft takes the toolkit's reading and shows $176.23 of premiums due on the Q3 wages paid after July 22; they were not withheld and cannot be taken from later paychecks. Under either reading nothing can now be taken from Omar Rasmussen. Under the toolkit's reading HANGS reports the wages as covered through September 30 and pays the $176.23 itself; under the statute's reading the wages are marked exempt from July 22 and nothing is due. A person decides which reading applies and files accordingly.

Tomas Arvelo has no contractor registration and no UBI on file, two of the conditions in RCW 50A.05.010. A person checks L&I's contractor-registration lookup and the Department of Revenue's business lookup for Tomas Arvelo: if either is missing, the exclusion fails on the facts and the work is covered; if both exist, whether the work was free from the foreman's control is the judgment. If the work is covered employment, $21,168.00 of wages and 504 hours belong on this report: $239.20 of Paid Leave premium and $122.77 of WA Cares premium.

Unsigned draft. The report was due November 2, 2026 (October 31 was a Saturday) and nothing has been filed or paid. Overdue Paid Leave premiums draw 1% interest a month (since August 2026), and the Paid Leave late-fees page lists penalties for late reports as coming soon (see the rule checks). A person reviews and files it in the Paid Leave employer account and pays the two premiums separately.

rules.question: How many hours go on the report for hourly and salaried employees?
rules.whyItMatters: Hours count toward benefit eligibility; salaried employees are reported at 40 a week whatever the hours worked.
rules.excerpt: Each calendar quarter, employers must report to the department the wages paid and the associated hours for each employee. ... (1) Hourly employees. Report the total number of hours worked by each employee. (2) Employees on salary. Report forty hours for each week in which a salaried employee as defined in WAC 192-500-100 worked. ... (4) Overtime. Report the number of hours actually worked for which overtime pay or compensatory time is provided, without regard to the amount of wages or compensation paid.
matchPhrases: each calendar quarter, employers must report to the department the wages paid and the associated hours for each employee
hourly employees. report the total number of hours worked by each employee
report forty hours for each week in which a salaried employee as defined in wac 192-500-100 worked
report the number of hours actually worked for which overtime pay or compensatory time is provided, without regard to the amount of wages or compensation paid
rules.ruleOrLimit: The hours reported are the hours associated with the wages paid in the quarter (WAC 192-540-030(2)(d)). Hourly employees: the hours worked, with overtime counted as the hours actually worked. Salaried employees: 40 hours for each week worked.

rules.question: Who pays the WA Cares premium, and how is it collected?
rules.whyItMatters: WA Cares is an employee premium that the employer collects by payroll deduction and sends to ESD; HANGS has no share of its own.
rules.effective: RCW 50B.04.080 as amended by 2025 c 380 s 10.
rules.excerpt: (1) ... The initial premium rate is .58 percent of the individual's wages. Beginning January 1, 2026, and biennially thereafter, the premium rate shall be set by the pension funding council at a rate no greater than .58 percent. ... (2)(a) The employer must collect from the employees the premiums provided under this section through payroll deductions and remit the amounts collected to the employment security department. ... (3)(b) To the extent feasible, the employment security department shall use the premium assessment, collection, and reporting procedures in Title 50A RCW.

rules.ruleOrLimit: The employer collects WA Cares premiums from employees by payroll deduction and remits them to ESD, which uses the Paid Leave procedures; the rate is .58 percent and can be no greater.

rules.question: When does each WA Cares exemption on file take effect, and when must withholding stop?

rules.excerpt: If your exemption is approved ESD will mail you a copy of your exemption approval letter, which will indicate the date your exemption takes effect (the first day of the quarter after your application is approved). ... Once you provide your approval letter to your employer(s) and your exemption has taken effect (as indicated on your approval letter), they must stop withholding premiums. ... Those who had private long-term care insurance on or before Nov. 1, 2021, were able to apply for an exemption from the WA Cares Fund from Oct. 1, 2021, until Dec. 31, 2022. Those who applied for this exemption, and were approved, are permanently exempt from WA Cares. ... You can discontinue your private long-term care insurance exemption between Jan. 1, 2026, and June 30, 2028.

rules.question: Is the hourly concrete finishing billed by Tomas Arvelo, an individual, covered employment whose pay belongs on this report?
rules.whyItMatters: If the work is employment, $21,168.00 of Q3 pay is wages for both premiums.
rules.effective: RCW 50A.05.010, the version in effect until June 30, 2027.
rules.excerpt: (8)(a) "Employment" means personal service, of whatever nature, unlimited by any employment relationship as known to the common law or any other legal relationship performed for wages ... (b) "Employment" does not include: ... (iv) Services that require registration under chapter 18.27 RCW or licensing under chapter 19.28 RCW rendered by an individual when: (A) The individual has been and will continue to be free from control or direction over the performance of the service, both under the contract of service and in fact; ... (E) ... has registered for and received a unified business identifier number from the state of Washington; ... and (G) On the effective date of the contract of service, the individual has a valid contractor registration pursuant to chapter 18.27 RCW ... (29) "Wage" or "wages" means: (a) For the purpose of premium assessment, the remuneration paid by an employer to an employee.
matchPhrases: means personal service, of whatever nature, unlimited by any employment relationship as known to the common law
services that require registration under chapter 18.27 rcw or licensing under chapter 19.28 rcw rendered by an individual when
the individual has been and will continue to be free from control or direction over the performance of the service, both under the contract of service and in fact
has registered for and received a unified business identifier number from the state of washington
on the effective date of the contract of service, the individual has a valid contractor registration pursuant to chapter 18.27 rcw
for the purpose of premium assessment, the remuneration paid by an employer to an employee
rules.ruleOrLimit: Employment is any personal service for wages, beyond the common-law test. Work that needs a contractor registration is excluded only when all seven conditions (A) to (G) are met, including freedom from control, a UBI and a valid contractor registration. Wages for premiums are the remuneration paid.
rules.hangsApplication: The labor vendor file shows Tomas Arvelo, an individual, paid $21,168.00 through accounts payable in Q3 for 504 hours of concrete finishing at $42.00 an hour at Tideflats Cold Storage, under the HGC foreman. No contractor registration and no UBI are on file, so the file does not show conditions (E) and (G) met, and work under the HGC foreman does not show the freedom from control that (A) requires. The draft leaves the payments off the report; if the work is employment, $21,168.00 of wages and 504 hours belong on it, with $239.20 of Paid Leave premium at 1.13% and $122.77 of WA Cares premium at 0.58%, $361.97 in all.
